trust_decision.summary: Which classes a network peer may have instantiated by Java deserialization of a log event is decided by an allowlist in LoggingEventObjectInputStream.resolveClass. The listener binds to all interfaces and has no peer authentication.

landing_point.why: The summary names the Log Socket Collector and deserialization. This is the only ObjectInputStream.readObject in src/main, and the allowlist sits 30 lines below.

fix_sites.entry_point: OSGi DS @Activate (config org.apache.karaf.decanter.collector.log.socket); TCP listener on port 4560 (fix binds to hostname, default localhost)
TCP connection to log socket port (SocketRunnable.run); fix adds optional username/password handshake
same TCP connection; LoggingEventObjectInputStream ctor/resolveClass replaced by JEP 290 ObjectInputFilter
same TCP connection; allowlist isAllowedByDefault adjusted (Hashtable prefix, [Ljava.util.Map)
shipped config file (fix.diff:13-17 adds hostname/backlog/username/password keys, commented)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changes are in one file plus its cfg. Activation (bind address) is the only site outside the deserializer, at collector/log4j-socket/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/decanter/collector/log/socket/SocketCollector.java:78.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the bind address (port open on all interfaces, SocketCollector.java:78) and the missing authentication are deployment or configuration matters, not deserialization, and keep only the class filter. Changing the default bind would also break remote log4j clients.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate log4j 1.x LoggingEvent with MDC Hashtable, String[] throwable rep and LocationInfo must still deserialize and be posted to EventAdmin. Unauthenticated clients must keep working when no username/password is configured (testNoAuthentication). A filter that is too tight (e.g. dropping java.util.Hashtable or [Ljava.lang.String) breaks MDC/throwable events.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: JMS listener that accepts ObjectMessage and calls getObject() alongside the TextMessage/unmarshaller path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: JMS collectors commonly accept ObjectMessage for Java producers. A maintainer adding it would not reuse the log-socket filter, which lives in another module.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 'java' data-format option in the generic TCP/UDP socket collector that reads frames with ObjectInputStream
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This collector already picks an unmarshaller by data format. A second Java-serialization front end in another package is a plausible second_implementation at distance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Java-serialization Unmarshaller implementation shared by kafka/mqtt/jms/rest collectors
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Unmarshaller SPI is pluggable by format. A binary 'java' unmarshaller would reach many transports without the log-socket filter.

O9_family: CWE-502 insecure deserialization (Java native serialization over an unauthenticated TCP listener)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven, JDK 11 (pom.xml:38 maven.compiler.target=11; the fix needs java.io.ObjectInputFilter, JDK 9+)
O10_build.project_tests: collector/log4j-socket/src/test/java/org/apache/karaf/decanter/collector/log/socket/SocketCollectorTest.java (JUnit4, local socket and stub EventAdmin). testUnknownEvent is @Ignore at the pinned commit (line 93).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten the resolveClass allowlist (e.g. exact names instead of 'java.lang.' prefix) and stop. This leaves the listener on all interfaces with no authentication, and leaves resolveProxyClass and graph limits unfiltered.

out_of_scope_notes: The generic socket collector defaults host to 0.0.0.0 with no auth, but it uses a JSON or raw unmarshaller, not Java deserialization (collector/socket/src/main/java/org/apache/karaf/decanter/collector/socket/SocketCollector.java:78).
The published allowlist still admits every 'java.lang.' prefixed class, including java.lang.reflect/java.lang.invoke subpackages (fix.diff:239). Not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check performed).
Advisory text itself was not available; trust decision inferred from the summary and the fix diff.

The pinned resolveClass override does not cover resolveProxyClass (SocketCollector.java:235-241 only), and the JEP 290 filter would also see proxy classes. Not confirmed whether this was the exploited gap or whether the advisory relies on bind/auth only.
Whether the pinned allowlist was actually bypassable (vs the advisory treating bind-all + no auth as the flaw) is not established from code alone.
present_in_latest not applicable: no O8 routes; latest release is 'none'.
